note_tweet.text:
Today we’re open-sourcing Inworld's Voice Isolator and SAVA (Semantic-Acoustic Voice Activity) models, and publishing the technical report behind Realtime TTS-2.

1/ Voice Isolator: preserve the speaker’s voice.

It removes background chatter, music, and noise while retaining the laughs, breaths, and character of the original recording. It works at 48 kHz, with an offline model for recordings and a realtime model that streams with 20 ms of lookahead.

2/ SAVA: give people room to finish their thought.

Our Semantic-Acoustic Voice Activity model uses both the sound and meaning of speech to detect when someone is speaking and when their turn is complete. It already runs in our voice products and fits on a single laptop CPU thread. In our tests on real meeting recordings, it detected completed turns in a median of 71 ms, compared with 210 ms for the open-source model we tested against.

3/ TTS-2 technical report: share how we built the voice on the other end.

We explain how we trained TTS-2 to follow instructions about delivery, use the same reference voice across languages, and generate streaming speech. We also cover the work behind Flash’s faster, more efficient serving, with training methods, evaluation results, and lessons from failures during development.

Voice Isolator and SAVA include code and model weights under Apache 2.0.

Explore the releases and try them on your own audio here: https://t.co/d6Wzu8aboi

Inworld Realtime TTS-2 and Realtime TTS-2 Flash sit near the top of @ArtificialAnlys's new Time to First Audio (TTFA) benchmark.

The benchmark measures how quickly models begin producing audible speech. In the latest results:

- 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝗧𝗧𝗦-𝟮 𝗙𝗹𝗮𝘀𝗵: 86ms on average

Thanks to the Artificial Analysis team for expanding its speech evaluations and sharing the methodology.

Our Head of Research, @altsoph, shared an experiment in “breeding” synthetic voices to bring more variety to our TTS library.

He used Inworld Voice Design to generate voices from text descriptions, then had an LLM modify and combine those descriptions based on evaluation results. Each generation was tested for quality and how different it sounded from voices already in the collection.

After 26 iterations, 214 voices passed automated checks, and human assessors selected 12 for the library.

Read the full piece to explore Aleksey’s process and hear some of the voices: https://t.co/1sA23021gm

note_tweet.text:
Today we’re introducing Reasoning for Realtime TTS-2, making it the first TTS model in the world that can steer itself based on context. 

In consumer apps, your LLM generates every reply. Directing how each one sounds takes extra prompts, tags, and rules.

Reasoning now handles that inside your TTS request. It reads the text and the context you pass, writes a delivery direction, which Realtime TTS-2 performs.

For developers this means:
- Emotion, tone, and pacing shaped by the context of each line.
- No emotion-tag rules to maintain in your chat prompt.
- Fewer LLM output tokens spent writing voice directions.

The generated direction comes back in the API response, so you can inspect it. Your own instructions and inline tags always take precedence.

Available today with Realtime TTS-2. Who are you building for?

Our @livekit partner story explores how Inworld’s speech models and LiveKit’s realtime infrastructure help developers build voice applications that can scale with their users.

Through Inworld’s integration with the LiveKit Agents framework, developers can use pre-built or custom voices alongside their choice of LLM and speech recognition models, with LiveKit handling realtime communication across web and mobile apps.

The accompanying video takes a closer look at expressive delivery, including how TTS-2’s voice steering helped the team bring Expressive Mode to LiveKit Agents. 

“Inworld's TTS-2 marks a real step forward in emotionally expressive voice synthesis. When combined with the conversational intelligence of LiveKit agents, it enables interactions that feel genuinely human, responsive, nuanced, and alive in ways that feel natural.” - David Zhao, CTO, LiveKit

Watch the video or read the full partner story for more on our work together: https://t.co/4MTeupx93h
